chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who came across an absconding slave, so he seized him, and the slave escaped from him. He (peace be upon him) said: 'There is nothing upon him.' I said, 'Supposing he came across a slave girl who had stolen from a neighbour of his, so he seized her in order to bring her to him, and she died.' (He (peace be upon him) said): 'There is nothing upon him.'

key_terms.ليس عليه شيء: There is nothing upon him (no liability)

ai.seo_question: What is the legal ruling if a person captures a runaway slave who then escapes or dies?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the captor incurs no liability (daman) if the runaway slave escapes or dies, provided the capture was for the legitimate purpose of restitution. This ruling underscores the principle of 'ease' in Islamic jurisprudence, relieving the individual of burden during the active pursuit of property rights. It reflects the practical legal standards of the early Shia community regarding possession and risk allocation in slave ownership.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a man who came across an absconding slave, so he seized him, and the slave escaped from him. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is nothing upon him’. I said, ‘Supposing he came across a slave girl who had stolen from a neighbour of his, so he seizes in order to come over with her, so she dies’. (He<sup>asws</sup> said): ‘There is nothing upon him’.
